correctness.rationale: Every possible two-length binary Kraft-equality word set is encoded uniquely by a three-bit subset S and a four-bit subset T. The seven combinatorial candidate counts sum to 1,901,636, all examined using independent literal Sardinas--Patterson string sets and bitmask residual-graph methods. They agree on all seven UD totals and every exceptional code; direct residual sets and de Bruijn strong-connectivity arguments verify the structural claims. Exhaustive finite enumeration is not extrapolated beyond this domain.

value.rationale: The exact number of uniquely decodable maximal-by-Kraft codes for a fixed natural length distribution is explicitly motivated in the coding literature; general inequalities do not determine it. The complete 512-element classification proves that 508 classical prefix/suffix designs are joined by exactly four exceptional mixed designs in a single orbit, and gives a complete decoder-class division. This is a mathematically interpretable equality-case classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a routine perturbation.
